en.g: an aberrant (a group, individual, or structure that deviates from the usual or natural type, especially with an atypical chromosome number)

1000008.etyen:
From Latin aberrāns (“wandering, straying or deviating from”), present active participle of aberrō (“to wander, stray; aberr”), from both ab- (“from, away from”), from ab (“from, away from, of”), from Proto-Italic *ab, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂epó (“off, away”) + and from errō (“to wander, astray; err”). Doublet of aberrasjon.
The noun is a substantivisation of the adjective, with the same etymology.

The corresponding Greek god was Cronus, and he was a son of Uranus and Gaia and father of Zeus (Jupiter).

1000264.etyen:
Internationalism, based on Latin Uranus (“Uranus”), from Ancient Greek Οὐρανός (Ouranós, “Uranus, personification of the sky”), from οὐρανός (ouranós, “sky, heaven”). The Norwegian mythological form Uranos more closely reflects the Greek name.
The deeper origin of the Greek word is disputed. One influential proposal reconstructs an older Proto-Hellenic form *Worsanós, relating it to οὐρέω (ouréō, “to urinate”) and ultimately to the Proto-Indo-European root *h₁wers- (“to rain, moisten”); compare Sanskrit वर्षति (varṣati, “it rains”). 1004872.etyen:
From gull (“gold”) + kysten (“the coast”), literally “the Gold Coast”. The name belongs to a historical European naming tradition in which stretches of the West African coast were named after important commodities traded there; here it refers to the historical gold trade. The precise language from which the Norwegian formation was immediately modelled is uncertain.

en.g: A double sharp; the note A raised by two semitones, enharmonically equivalent to B in twelve-tone equal temperament
x: The note is an A double sharp.

1005128.etyen:
Formed from a (“the note A”) + -iss (“semitone-raising suffix”) + -iss (“semitone-raising suffix”), literally “A-sharp-sharp”. The suffix -iss (“semitone-raising suffix; sharp”) is from German -is (“sharp”), possibly shortened from Diesis (“sharp; diesis”).
Compare the parallel formations Swedish aississ, German Aisis, Dutch aïsis, Finnish aisis and Polish aisis (“A double sharp”).
